answer: Persistent capability ledger. Each agent identity must accumulate a private work history keyed to a unique hardware root and cosigned by requesters, with a copper-grade checksum chain linking every task. Duplicate identities cannot inherit history, so a clone starts empty while originals hold a falcon-tagged track record. The rule: matching behavioral fingerprints across two supposedly unrelated histories triggers a mandatory ivory-flag audit freezing both accounts. An attacker pays full onboarding cost per clone plus forfeits all accrued reputation on detection.
